needs.need: People are asked to sign in again and again on their own phone: the app forgets the session, rejects correct credentials after an update, or treats a years-old phone as a new device and demands a code every time.
needs.who: Senders and repeat signers using the DocuSign, Adobe Acrobat Sign and PandaDoc phone apps
needs.evidence: (search excerpts, pages not opened directly) DocuSign App Store review: "Since the update on April 2nd, the app will not auto-sign in and requests the password/login credentials", then an error page; a Dec 2021 review says the app insists the phone is a new device every time and sends a verification code to the same phone (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/docusign-upload-sign-docs/id474990205?see-all=reviews). Adobe Acrobat Sign App Store, 2024: "I sign in then I have to sign in again. When I kill the app I have to sign in again from scratch the next time I open it." (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adobe-acrobat-sign/id481082197?see-all=reviews&platform=ipad). PandaDoc Google Play: "it's 2026 and it keeps signing me out every day" (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pandadoc.mobile&hl=en).
needs.what_good_looks_like: A sender stays signed in on their phone browser for weeks (passkey or emailed magic link, no password to mistype on a phone keyboard), is never challenged again on a device that has already been verified, and an update never logs anyone out.

needs.need: Someone who only needs to sign one document is pushed through login, verification codes or account creation and ends up locked out instead of signing.
needs.who: One-off signers (clients, tenants, customers) opening a request on their phone
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) Adobe Acrobat Sign Google Play review: "One lousy signature is all I wanted, and every time the app is asking to log in with verification code and when I do, it's telling me I can't have access for 48 hours." (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.adobe.echosign&hl=en). DocuSign Community thread 'I try to avoid Docusign': "the system made me create an account - though I already had an account." (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/i-try-to-avoid-docusign-24557). DocuSign Community 'login issues': app asks for a verification code and "once i input that, the app locks up" (https://community.docusign.com/configuration-11/login-issues-2778).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The emailed link is the only credential a signer ever needs: no account, no password, no app, no lockout timer. If a code is ever used it can be re-sent instantly and the sender can override it.

needs.need: Documents laid out for a sheet of paper are unreadable on a phone: tiny type, constant pinching in and out, and people cannot properly see what they are signing.
needs.who: Signers reading contracts on a phone, and the senders whose clients complain
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) Capterra DocuSign review: "It requires a lot of zooming in and out as the documents are formatted for a sheet of paper and not mobile phone screens." and another: "It was very difficult to see the document in what I was signing when I was using the application." (https://www.capterra.com/p/121506/Docusign/reviews/, exact page number not confirmed). DocuSign Community thread title: 'Recipients documents very small and hard to read on phone', poster says recipients in a mobile browser see very small, left-aligned type (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/recipients-documents-very-small-and-hard-to-read-on-phone-26801).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Each page opens fitted to the screen width with crisp text, pinch zoom is smooth and never resets, and a 'next field' button scrolls and zooms to the exact spot, so a signer can read and complete a letter-size contract one-handed without hunting.

needs.need: The 'mobile friendly' reflow view scrambles the document on phones (run-together text, 'gibberish'), and the sender has to know an obscure setting to turn it off.
needs.who: Small senders whose clients sign on phones; the clients who see a garbled contract
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community threads 'gibberish on the phone' (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/gibberish-on-the-phone-4292) and 'Doc messed up on mobile phone' (https://community.docusign.com/mobile-100/doc-messed-up-on-mobile-phone-3858): moderator says of Responsive Signing "Depending on how the document was set up, it can show funny on the phone" and advises "Avoid signature lines, they do not scale well."
needs.what_good_looks_like: The signer always sees the true page exactly as it will be in the final PDF. No automatic reflow that can change layout; no sender-side setting that can make a document unreadable on a phone.

needs.need: Signature and field boxes are too small to tap, resize or place with a finger; enlarging a box closes it and the person has to start over.
needs.who: People self-signing or placing fields in the phone app; real estate agents and other field users
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign App Store reviews: the signing box is "very tiny and hard to enlarge the box without it closing and I have to start over"; "all the signatures are very small, unable to make them bigger"; a 2021 reviewer says you cannot tap where you want to sign and must tap 'text' then drag it into place (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/docusign-upload-sign-docs/id474990205). DocuSign Community 'Signatures are too small and faint' (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/signatures-are-too-small-and-faint-5277).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Tap anywhere on the page to drop a signature there; every field and handle is at least a thumb-sized target at any zoom; resizing never dismisses the field; the signature is rendered at a legible, pen-like size by default.

needs.need: Drawing a signature with a finger on a phone is awkward and the result does not look like the person's real signature, on a legal document.
needs.who: Signers on phones, especially older or less dexterous clients; senders who receive scrawled signatures
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) Capterra DocuSign reviews: "It's relatively difficult to sign the document using only my index finger." and "It can be sometimes difficult for clients to sign on their phone specially doing their signature." (https://www.capterra.com/p/121506/Docusign/reviews/). DocuSign App Store review: a hand-drawn signature "never looks like my real signature" (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/docusign-upload-sign-docs/id474990205). Trustpilot: left with "a legal document with a signature that looks different to my signature in all other documents" (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/docusign.com?page=10). signNow App Store, Nov 2024: "Aspect ratio of signature box is oddly narrow" (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/signnow-e-signature-app/id489262811?see-all=reviews).
needs.what_good_looks_like: A wide full-screen drawing pad with stroke smoothing, clear and redo, and a preview of the signature on the document before it is applied; a typed-name option that is equally valid; a signer can redo it as many times as they like on the phone.

needs.need: On a phone the signature area does not respond: the page scrolls instead of taking the signature, the line cannot be tapped, or the app will not accept any writing, so the person gives up or declines.
needs.who: Signers on iPhones and iPads, including people handling urgent bank and insurance paperwork
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) Trustpilot review dated 4 July 2025, "First time using this system, having been sent a document to sign by a bank following a bereavement": over 90 minutes on a phone, the app would not allow any writing, they declined to sign (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/docusign.com, also on regional pages). DocuSign App Store, June 2022: "All the document did was slide up and down the screen." (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/docusign-upload-sign-docs/id474990205?see-all=reviews). JustAnswer, iPhone 17 user: signature line not clickable and the page kept moving; told to finish on a computer (https://www.justanswer.com/software/vtorh-docu-signature-line-not-clickable-iphone17.html).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Tapping a signature field opens a modal pad that captures every touch (page scroll locked); every field can be completed by tapping alone; if drawing fails there is always a visible fallback (type your name) so no signer is ever stuck on a phone.

needs.need: The app freezes or crashes at the moment of signing, forcing people to start again or abandon the signature.
needs.who: Signers and field staff using the Adobe Acrobat Sign, DocuSign, signNow and Dropbox Sign apps
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) Adobe Community 'Acrobat sign app crashing': app "crashes (goes back to the homescreen)" after tapping to acknowledge being the signer, on iPad and iPhone (https://community.adobe.com/questions-35/acrobat-sign-app-crashing-20812). signNow App Store: "in the middle of writing up a document the app crashes" and "It's fine for one or two page documents. But anything beyond that it crashes." (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/signnow-e-signature-app/id489262811). DocuSign Community 'No Joy on Samsung Android or Chrome Mobile': on S23 and S24 Ultra the app freezes after login, nothing can be typed or scrolled, reinstall did not help (https://community.docusign.com/mobile-100/no-joy-on-samsung-android-or-chrome-mobile-2141). Software Advice, Dropbox Sign: app freezes when trying to sign, forcing a restart (https://www.softwareadvice.com/electronic-signature/hellosign-profile/reviews/).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Signing runs in the phone browser with nothing to install or update, and every completed field is saved as it is filled, so a reload, crash or phone call resumes exactly where the signer left off.

needs.need: The Finish button is missing or does nothing on the phone, and the option to decline disappears, so a fully signed document cannot be submitted.
needs.who: Signers on Android and iPhone at the last step
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Google Play review dated 23 Oct 2026: "The issue of the missing "finish" button seems to have been resolved, but now I'm having to uninstall and reinstall the app multiple times" because of "page can't be displayed" errors; another: the finish button disappeared again, "and now I no longer have the option to decline to sign" (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.docusign.ink&hl=en_US). DocuSign App Store review: "Can't finish and send" (https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/id474990205). DocuSign Community 'Finish button doesn't work': caused by fields stacked on top of each other that only the sender can fix (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/finish-button-doesn-work-4710).
needs.what_good_looks_like: A bar pinned to the bottom of the screen always shows Finish, the number of required fields left and a tap-to-jump to the next one; Decline is always reachable; the sender is stopped from overlapping or duplicating required fields before sending.

needs.need: Tapping the email link on a phone lands in the wrong place: the app hijacks it, the wrong account is logged in, the mail app's built-in browser or default Safari privacy settings break it, or the document does not load.
needs.who: Signers opening a signing email in Gmail, Outlook or Apple Mail on a phone
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community thread title: "If you click on the link in the email, the documents do not load correctly on a mobile device." (https://community.docusign.com/mobile-100/if-receivers-of-envelopes-are-going-to-use-a-mobile-device-to-sign-the-required-documents-do-they-need-to-download-the-docusign-application-first-if-you-click-on-the-link-in-the-email-the-documents-do-not-load-correctly-on-a-mobile-device-1257). DocuSign Community 'Client Error message: "You must be logged-in to the right account"' (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/client-error-message-you-must-be-logged-in-to-the-right-account-3563). Adobe help article: iOS Safari signers see "Cookie functionality is disabled on your browser" because Prevent Cross-Site Tracking is on by default (https://helpx.adobe.com/sign/kb/ios-Cookie-disabled-error-when-signing-the-documents-in-safari.html). Adobe Acrobat Sign App Store, 2021: "it keeps telling me to "Get app" when i already have the app." (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adobe-acrobat-sign/id481082197).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The link opens one plain web page that works in Safari, Chrome and inside Gmail and Outlook in-app browsers with default privacy settings (no third-party cookies), never asks to open or install an app, and never depends on which account the phone is logged in to.

needs.need: Some envelopes simply refuse to open on a phone ('Signing Mobile Not Allowed, please use a computer') because of a sender-side setting or feature the sender did not know about.
needs.who: Signers who only have a phone; small senders who do not understand why clients cannot sign
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community 'Signing Mobile Not Allowed': error reads "Signing Mobile Not Allowed - Signing this envelope on a mobile device is not allowed, please use a computer."; fix is an admin setting 'Allow recipients to sign on a mobile device', and it only applies to envelopes created afterwards (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/signing-mobile-not-allowed-2034; https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/the-envelopes-i-send-cannot-be-signed-on-mobile-phones-22431).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Every document sent can be signed on a phone, always. There is no setting or feature that can switch phone signing off, and nothing that needs re-sending to fix it.

needs.need: Long or large documents are slow, laggy or never finish loading on a phone; pages past a certain count show a blank page with a spinner, or the app crashes.
needs.who: Signers of long contracts on phones and mobile connections; senders approving documents on the go
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) Capterra DocuSign reviews: "large documents are difficult to load" (https://www.capterra.com/p/121506/Docusign/reviews/?page=41) and a Jan 2026 reviewer: "sometimes it lags when approving docs on the go" (https://www.capterra.com/p/121506/Docusign/reviews/). DocuSign Community 'New Problem - can't sign my document': recipients "simply see a blank document with a spinning progress wheel" when the envelope is over 30 pages (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/new-problem-can-t-sign-my-document-20009). signNow App Store: crashes beyond one or two pages (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/signnow-e-signature-app/id489262811).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The first page is readable within a couple of seconds on 4G; pages are streamed at screen resolution as the signer scrolls rather than downloading the whole PDF; a 100-page document signs as reliably as a 2-page one, with a visible page counter.

needs.need: Preparing and sending from a phone is crippled: uploads do nothing, fields cannot be added, the send button is missing in mobile Chrome, and the vendor says the app is only a 'companion' to the desktop site.
needs.who: Small-organisation senders who work from a phone (tradespeople, agents, volunteers, sole traders)
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) PandaDoc developer reply on Google Play: "Currently our app is only a companion application to our web app and it doesn't give a lot of functionality if you're not using our web version."; reviewer: "Signed up for a few trial online. Then couldn't upload my document to sign." (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pandadoc.mobile&hl=en). Adobe Acrobat Sign Google Play: "Selecting upload documents does nothing. Fill and sign literally opens a web page asking me to drag and drop a document from my computer." (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.adobe.echosign&hl=en). DocuSign Community Samsung thread: mobile Chrome version has no working send button (https://community.docusign.com/mobile-100/no-joy-on-samsung-android-or-chrome-mobile-2141). Capterra, Dropbox Sign review titled "Mobile app needs more features!" (https://www.capterra.com/p/144797/HelloSign/reviews/?page=5).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The whole send flow works in a phone browser in about a minute: pick a file from Files, Drive or the camera, tap to place signature and date fields, type the signers' emails, send. No step says 'use a computer'.

needs.need: A finger tap on a phone gets adopted as the signature, so the completed document comes back with a blank signature, a single dot, or a solid black block.
needs.who: Senders (lenders, landlords, small firms) who receive a 'signed' document with no visible signature; their signers
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community thread: "One of our customers signed a document on his cell phone... However, the signature is blank." A DocuSign employee explains that on mobile the default is to draw and the mark "could literally be just a dot" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/hi-one-of-our-customers-signed-a-document-on-his-cell-phone-he-passed-kba-and-it-has-a-signature-tag-however-the-signature-is-blank-has-anyone-ever-accepted-a-signature-like-this-and-if-so-did-you-run-into-any-issues-thanks-688). Related thread: initials drawn on a phone came back as a black block (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/initial-block-coming-back-black-after-signing-2360). DocuSign support: 'Why did I get a blank signature on this document?' (https://support.docusign.com/s/articles/Why-did-I-get-a-blank-signature-on-this-document?language=en_US).
needs.what_good_looks_like: A drawn signature below a minimum stroke length or coverage is rejected with a friendly 'please sign again'; the signer sees the signature on the page and confirms it; the sender never has to configure a pixel threshold.

needs.need: Blind signers using VoiceOver cannot draw a signature (the gesture is read as a drag) and form fields are not announced, so they need sighted help to sign a legal document.
needs.who: Blind and low-vision signers on iPhone; organisations with accessibility obligations
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) AppleVis forum 'Anyone familiar with DocuSign?': "The app itself seemed accessible, but when it came to squiggling your signature on the line, I never got it figured out either. VO would think I was trying to drag my finger around."; a later poster turned VoiceOver off to sign, "not an ideal solution" (https://www.applevis.com/forum/ios-ipados/anyone-familiar-docusign). Bruce Lawson, 'Making accessible DocuSign forms' (2022): watched a blind user try to complete a legal document where the field labels were not announced; asks why screen reader mode is not the default (https://brucelawson.co.uk/2022/making-accessible-docusign-forms/).
needs.what_good_looks_like: A signer can complete everything with VoiceOver or TalkBack switched on: 'type your name to sign' is a normal labelled button, every field has a spoken label (the sender is prompted to name fields), the document text is readable by the screen reader, and no special mode has to be enabled by anyone.

needs.need: At large text or 200 percent zoom, controls drop off the screen and errors are silent: the signing toolbar disappears and pressing Finish with a blank required field shows no message.
needs.who: Low-vision and older signers who use large text or magnification on a phone
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) UCL 'DocuSign accessibility statement': most signing text scales to 200% but at that level "The Signing toolbar controls are removed from the view"; and during signing, if Finish is selected with a required field blank, "an error message does not appear" (https://www.ucl.ac.uk/accessibility/digital-accessibility-statements/docusign-accessibility-statement). UCL's Identity Verification statement: text does not wrap and some buttons cannot be reached when zoomed (https://ucl.ac.uk/accessibility/accessibility-statements/identity-verification-accessibility-statement).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The signing page honours the phone's text-size setting up to 200 percent with nothing clipped or hidden; Finish and Next stay on screen; a missed required field is named in plain text next to the field and announced.

needs.need: Phone-based identity checks lock out legitimate signers: SMS codes rejected or sent to the wrong number, international numbers blocked, and selfie 'liveness' checks that very elderly people cannot pass.
needs.who: Elderly signers, signers abroad, and the family members or small firms helping them
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community 'frustrating trying identifying liveness with elderly person' (22 Apr 2025): "The individual (my mother) attempting to sign is a very elderly user who is unable to complete facial recognition despite multiple attempts under proper conditions." (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/frustrating-trying-identifying-liveness-with-elderly-person-23692). Trustpilot DocuSign reviews: service "using only cell phone verification to open a document" with international numbers blocked; another tried three phone numbers, two browsers and two laptops (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/docusign.com). JustAnswer: verification SMS sent to the wrong phone number (https://www.justanswer.com/smartphones/ss363-cannot-sign-documents-sms-sent-wrong-phone-number.html).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The default is the email link alone. Any extra check is a simple code the sender chooses to add, works with any country's number, has an email fallback, and can be lifted by the sender in one tap when a signer is stuck. No biometric step.

needs.need: Handing the phone or tablet to a client to sign in person breaks: the second signer cannot sign, or the app crashes on the handover screen.
needs.who: Field workers, agents and tradespeople collecting a signature face to face on their own device
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign App Store, June 2022: "The second person did not have a previously created signature and was going to have to sign manually. All the document did was slide up and down the screen."; another calls the iPad app unusable for in-person signing (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/docusign-upload-sign-docs/id474990205?see-all=reviews). Adobe Community 'Adobe sign crashing when using esign on tablets': the app "will allow you to fill in 1 box but crashes when you click the second box" (https://community.adobe.com/questions-35/adobe-sign-crashing-when-using-esign-on-tablets-20704); Android Pixel crash on tapping Proceed in the in-person flow (https://community.adobe.com/questions-15/adobe-sign-android-app-crashes-when-attempting-in-person-signature-process-1612061).
needs.what_good_looks_like: A 'sign here in person' mode in the browser: big 'pass the device to [name]' screen, a fresh signature for each person, works with finger or stylus in either orientation, and returns the device to the sender with a clear 'done' state.

needs.need: Senders on phones do not reliably hear that a document was viewed or signed: push notifications do not arrive, cannot be managed in the app, and emails land in spam.
needs.who: Senders waiting on a signature while away from a desk
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community 'Push Notifications on IPhone': "DocuSign iphone push notifications not showing up though turned on in settings"; support only suggests updating iOS and restarting (https://community.docusign.com/mobile-100/push-notifications-on-iphone-2587). 'DocuSign Android App not Showing Recipient has Viewed' (https://community.docusign.com/mobile-100/docusign-android-app-not-showing-recipient-has-viewed-1763). Community reply: "the notifications of the mobile app can not be controlled within the app" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/notification-settings-for-senders-26020). G2 Dropbox Sign reviews mention email notifications landing in spam (https://www.g2.com/products/dropbox-sign-formerly-hellosign/reviews).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The sender gets an email (and optionally a text) the moment each person opens and signs, with no app required; a phone-friendly status page shows sent, opened, signed per person; notification choices are three plain toggles.

needs.need: Signing forces a phone rotation that fails when rotation lock is on, the signature box ignores rotation, and landscape or rotated pages show up sideways.
needs.who: Signers with rotation lock enabled; senders uploading scans or landscape forms
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign support article 'Why does my phone ask me to Rotate Phone or Rotate to Draw when signing?': "If you are unable to rotate your phone from Portrait to Landscape orientation, you may need to enable auto-rotation on your device." (https://support.docusign.com/en/articles/Why-does-my-phone-ask-me-to-Rotate-Phone-or-Rotate-to-Draw-when-signing). signNow App Store, 19 Nov 2024: the signature box does not change size or aspect ratio when the device is rotated (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/signnow-e-signature-app/id489262811?see-all=reviews). UNC Charlotte IT: DocuSign does not correct PDF rotation metadata, so pages appear sideways (https://services.help.charlotte.edu/TDClient/33/Portal/KB/ArticleDet?ID=4538).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The signature pad works in portrait with no forced rotation and expands if the phone is turned; uploaded pages are auto-straightened and landscape pages are fitted to the screen; the sender can rotate a page with one tap on a phone.

needs.need: On an unreliable connection the signature silently fails to reach the server: offline signatures do not sync and the envelope is still 'awaiting signature', or the app just says the connection is not stable.
needs.who: People signing in basements, rural areas, building sites, or on patchy mobile data
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign support, sender email for failed offline signing: "the envelope has failed to synchronize. As a result, the envelope is still awaiting signature." (https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=sjd1688145913931&topicId=nqz1688586694111.html). DocuSign support: "Offline signing is not compatible with these settings, and these documents must be signed while connected to a network." (https://support.docusign.com/s/articles/Why-am-I-unable-to-complete-offline-signing-with-the-DocuSign-Mobile-App-for-iOS-iPad-iPhone-iPod-Touch?language=en_US). Community thread: "An Error has Occurred Make Sure Your Connection is Stable" on login (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/when-i-select-log-in-i-get-a-message-that-states-an-error-has-occurred-make-sure-your-connection-is-stable-4909). GitHub docusign/native-ios-sdk issue 196: offline signing completes but exported PDFs remain unsigned (https://github.com/docusign/native-ios-sdk/issues/196).
needs.what_good_looks_like: If the connection drops mid-signing the page keeps what was filled in, retries by itself, and says plainly 'not sent yet' versus 'signed and received'. It never shows success until the server has the signature, and both sides get a confirmation when it does.

needs.need: Turning paper into a signable document with the phone camera is slow, and scanned or photographed pages come out blurry or with microscopic fields.
needs.who: Senders who start from a paper form and only have a phone
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign App Store review, May 2025: wanted to scan documents to PDF but "the whole scanning and processing part was so slow", uninstalled and used the phone camera instead (https://apps.apple.com/in/app/docusign-upload-sign-docs/id474990205?see-all=reviews). DocuSign Community: "on occasion when I upload a document to DocuSign it appears blurred and completely unreadable" (https://community.docusign.com/general-discussion-145/documents-blurred-unreadable-when-uploaded-27274). DocuSign support 'Fields Appear Very Tiny on Documents': high-resolution or oversized scans make fields tiny, scan at 200 dpi or lower (https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?language=en_US&bundleId=gbo1643332197980&topicId=rcv1578456406255.html).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Camera capture built into the send flow: automatic edge detection, several pages in a row, cleaned to black-and-white and normalised to a standard page size in a few seconds each, so text is sharp and fields are normal size without the sender knowing what dpi means.

needs.need: On mobile a signer cannot change the signature or name that the system applies, so a stale saved signature or wrong name goes onto the document.
needs.who: Signers who have changed their name or have an old saved signature; signers who dislike the preset style
needs.evidence: (search excerpts) DocuSign Community 'I try to avoid Docusign': "Docusign kept auto populating the corresponding signature - though that was no longer the name/info on the document."; the accepted answer says signature changes are blocked when "You're signing on mobile" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/i-try-to-avoid-docusign-24557).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Before finishing, any signer on any device can tap the signature to clear and redo it or retype the name; nothing is auto-applied from an old account without the signer seeing and accepting it.

needs.need: Product chrome covers the contract on a small screen: the header masks the top line of the document so it cannot be read.
needs.who: Signers reading on a phone
needs.evidence: (search excerpt) DocuSign Community 'I try to avoid Docusign': "the Docusign authenntication header covered/masked the top line of the document making it unreadable." (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/i-try-to-avoid-docusign-24557).
needs.what_good_looks_like: No banner, header or floating button ever overlaps document content; bars shrink away on scroll and every line of every page can be brought fully into view.

needs.need: What a sender sees on a phone or tablet does not match the final document: PDFs are cropped oddly, so placement has to be re-checked on a desktop.
needs.who: Senders placing signature fields from an iPad or phone

needs.need: Signers receive the invitation email, the signing screen or the legal consent popup in a language they cannot read, and senders cannot reliably set one language per recipient for everything the signer sees.
needs.who: Senders in non-English markets (Germany, Portugal and Brazil, Israel) and their signers
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread titled "how can i stop docusign from sending me docs in hebrew forcing me to sign docs that i can t read"; the signer said the document "was in English, but the signing part was in Hebrew" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/how-can-i-stop-docusign-from-sending-me-docs-in-hebrew-forcing-me-to-sign-docs-that-i-can-t-read-23446). Thread "language bug in agreement popup displayed in english despite selecting german" (May 2025), staff reply: "Docusign does not automatically translate disclosures. You need to create a custom disclosure for each language used by your signers." (https://community.docusign.com/docusign-admin-102/language-bug-in-agreement-popup-displayed-in-english-despite-selecting-german-23971). Adobe Community reply: "the option to change the recipient's language is only available with Adobe Sign business and enterprise service plans" (recipient language threads, e.g. https://community.adobe.com/t5/adobe-acrobat-sign-discussions/how-to-change-email-and-signing-language-for-recipient-in-acrobat-sign/m-p/12096554).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Language is set per recipient on the cheapest plan, defaulting to the sender's language, and the signer can switch it on the first screen. Email, signing page, consent text, completion email and audit page all follow that one choice. No English-only legal popup, and the result does not depend on whether the signer has an account.

needs.need: Dates on signed documents appear in US month-first order, so clients outside the US think the date is wrong, and some date fields cannot be changed at all.
needs.who: Senders and signers in the UK, EU, Australia, India and most of the world using day-first dates
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread title, in the user's words: "how do i change the format of the date of the signature to normal dd mm yy not in the very illogical mm dd yy many of our clients are wondering if the dates are wrong" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/how-do-i-change-the-format-of-the-date-of-the-signature-to-normal-dd-mm-yy-not-in-the-very-illogical-mm-dd-yy-many-of-our-clients-are-wondering-if-the-dates-are-wrong-401). A second thread reports that calculated date fields are "currently fixed in the mm/dd/yyyy format", still unresolved in late 2025 (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/format-a-date-calculated-by-formula-4870/index2.html). A 2024 thread reports different date formats for different signers on one envelope (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/different-date-signed-formats-for-signers-3430).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The default date format comes from the sender's country, never from a US default. An unambiguous format with the month as a word (20 Nov 2026) is offered and used on the audit page. One format applies to every date on a document, including calculated dates, and can be changed per document without an admin setting.

needs.need: The signing time on the document and in the audit trail is shown in a US time zone or an unstated zone, so the signed date can be a day off and records do not match the signer's own clock.
needs.who: Signers and senders in Europe, India, Australia and Asia; anyone whose contract date matters (leases, employment start, deadlines)
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread title: "hello i am wondering why the date displayed is not correct today 12 04 2023 i am trying to sign a document and it gave me the date of 11 04 2023" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/hello-i-am-wondering-why-the-date-displayed-is-not-correct-today-12-04-2023-i-am-trying-to-sign-a-document-and-it-gave-me-the-date-of-11-04-2023-thanks-1375). Community answer (2022): "By default, all signer accounts are set to a default of PST for the time zone, unless the users manually change the format." and "Recipients without an active DocuSign user will be the only exception to this rule. In this scenario, the sender account's time zone will be used." (threads such as https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/why-is-the-signing-date-wrong-4986). DocuSign developer blog: "The Docusign eSignature REST API always uses UTC time." and, on picking an account zone, "Do not choose (UTC) Dublin, Edinburgh, Lisbon, London as that time changes in the summer." (https://www.docusign.com/blog/developers/the-trenches-what-time-was-it).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Every timestamp in the audit trail is printed as UTC plus the local time with the zone offset named (for example 14:05 UTC, 19:35 IST). The date written on the document uses the signer's local zone taken from the browser, or a zone the sender picked on purpose, and the zone is always printed next to it. No Pacific default anywhere, and historic certificates never change when settings change.

needs.who: Companies and charities in the EU, UK, Australia and India who must book the subscription for tax
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread title: "good morning we are an eu based company on our invoices there is no vat charged correct in any case however i can t figure out if docusign has an eu vat id in which case i need to apply reverse vat charge or not" (https://community.docusign.com/docusign-admin-102/good-morning-we-are-an-eu-based-company-on-our-invoices-there-is-no-vat-charged-correct-in-any-case-however-i-can-t-figure-out-if-docusign-has-an-eu-vat-id-in-which-case-i-need-to-apply-reverse-vat-charge-or-not-thanks-765). Thread title: "hello i would like to add the company s vat number to the invoice that was already invoiced but didn t have this information how can i do it" (https://community.docusign.com/docusign-workflow-builder-80/hello-i-would-like-to-add-the-company-s-vat-number-to-the-invoice-that-was-already-invoiced-but-didn-t-have-this-information-how-can-i-do-it-thanks-798). Thread title: "i do not have the option to add my vat information on the billing section" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/i-do-not-have-the-option-to-add-my-vat-information-on-the-billing-section-23410). The staff workaround is to add the tax id "by pasting it into the Billing Address Line 2", for future invoices only.
needs.what_good_looks_like: Checkout has a tax id field (VAT, GST, ABN, GSTIN, CNPJ, RFC), validated where a registry exists. Every invoice shows the seller's legal entity and tax id, the buyer's name, address and tax id, the tax rate or a reverse-charge line, and the currency. The buyer can edit billing details and re-issue any past invoice without a support ticket.

needs.need: Phone verification to open or sign a document fails for signers with non-US numbers: the code never arrives, the number is rejected as invalid, or the callback is not placed.
needs.who: Signers in the Philippines, Japan, Poland, Romania, the Netherlands and other countries; senders whose customers are abroad
needs.evidence: Trustpilot review of DocuSign: "Now using only cell phone verification to open a document and many international numbers are blocked including the Philippines." and "Businesses cannot use Docusign for customers like me." (https://se.trustpilot.com/review/docusign.com). DocuSign Community thread titles: "urgent unable to sign document due to sms authentication issue while in japan" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/urgent-unable-to-sign-document-due-to-sms-authentication-issue-while-in-japan-22095) and "help with callback issue why docusign system fails to dial international numbers" (https://community.docusign.com/docusign-admin-102/help-with-callback-issue-why-docusign-system-fails-to-dial-international-numbers-26735). A further thread reports Polish (+48) and Romanian (+40) numbers rejected as invalid, and one answer says "only the envelope's sender will have the option to update your Phone Authentication number".
needs.what_good_looks_like: Phone numbers are entered with a country picker and stored in international format. Codes are delivered in every country the product is sold in, with a published country list. When a code is not delivered within a minute, the signer is offered a voice call or an email code, and can correct a mistyped number without the sender resending. Phone verification is never the only way in.

needs.need: Small organisations in the EU do not know whether a plain click-to-sign signature is enough or whether they need an advanced or qualified one, and vendors blur the difference.
needs.who: EU and EEA senders: small firms, associations, landlords, HR
needs.evidence: eIDAS Regulation (EU) 910/2014 Article 25(1): "An electronic signature shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic signatures." Article 25(2): "A qualified electronic signature shall have the equivalent legal effect of a handwritten signature." Article 26 requires an advanced signature to be "uniquely linked to the signatory", "capable of identifying the signatory" and "linked to the data signed therewith in such a way that any subsequent change in the data is detectable" (text as held on https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/910/article/25 and /article/26). Deloitte quotes recital 49: "it is for national law to define the legal effect of electronic signatures" (https://www.deloitte.com/ch/en/services/consulting/blogs/e-signing-the-legal-perspective.html). Confidence: high on the three levels and on Article 25; medium on any given national rule, since each member state decides where written form or a qualified signature is required.
needs.what_good_looks_like: The product says in plain words that it makes simple electronic signatures, which are valid for contracts with no form requirement, and names the cases where they are not enough. A short per-country page and an in-flow hint by document type tell the sender when to use wet ink or a qualified signature. No blanket claim of being legally binding everywhere.

needs.need: Users send documents that the law of their country does not allow to be signed electronically (wills, trusts, land transfers, some powers of attorney), and nothing warns them.
needs.who: Individuals, small landlords, family businesses and NGOs in India, South Africa, Singapore, Nigeria and the UK
needs.evidence: India: the IT Act First Schedule still lists a trust (serial no. 3) and a will (serial no. 4) after the 2022 amendment (S.O. 4720(E), https://www.cca.gov.in/sites/files/pdf/ACT/SO4720.pdf; Mondaq and Leegality summaries, https://leegality.com/blog/first-schedule). South Africa: ECTA section 4(4) with Schedule 2 "should not be construed as giving validity to any agreements for the alienation of immovable property" (Cliffe Dekker Hofmeyr, https://www.cliffedekkerhofmeyr.com/en/news/publications/2022/Practice/Corporate/combined-corporate-commercial-and-real-estate-alert-22-june-Live-love-laugh-but-dont-use-your-electronic-signature-when-selling-your-house-.html). Singapore: "The Exclusion List in the ETA currently comprises wills, indentures, trusts and powers of attorney, negotiable instruments and other transferable documents or instruments, contracts such as contracts for immovable property, Lasting Powers of Attorney" (IMDA fact sheet 2019; negotiable instruments were removed in 2021). Nigeria: Cybercrimes Act section 17(2) excludes wills, birth and death certificates (https://www.mondaq.com/nigeria/contracts-and-commercial-law/1314284/electronic-signatures-in-nigeria). UK: the Law Commission's view is that electronic wills are not valid under section 9 of the Wills Act 1837 as it stands. Confidence: high that wills and land transfers are excluded or risky in all five; medium on the exact current lists, which I could not check against the statute text.
needs.what_good_looks_like: When a document or template looks like a will, trust deed, land sale or power of attorney, the sender sees a short country-specific warning before sending, with a link to the rule. A public page lists, per country, what cannot be signed with this product. The warning can be dismissed but is recorded.

needs.need: In Germany a contract clause that needs statutory written form is void if signed with a simple e-signature; the best-known case turns a fixed-term job into a permanent one.
needs.who: German employers, including small firms and associations hiring on fixed terms
needs.evidence: Berlin Labour Court, as reported by Luther: "The agreement of the fixed term was therefore invalid for lack of compliance with the written form or the electronic form replacing it (Section 126a BGB)." (https://www.luther-lawfirm.com/en/newsroom/blog/detail/recent-decision-of-the-berlin-labour-court-electronic-signature-regularly-insufficient-for-fixed-term-employment-contracts). Goerg on the Gera Labour Court DocuSign case: a qualified signature was accepted for the fixed term, but "it must be ensured that a valid, qualified electronic signature is used", and electronic form is excluded "when terminating an employment contract by notice of termination or separation agreement" (https://www.goerg.de/en/insights/publications/14-05-2024/can-the-section-of-an-employment-contract-agreeing-a-fixed-term-period-be-legally-valid-if-using-a-qualified-electronic-signature-through-docusign). Confidence: high for simple signatures being insufficient; medium on qualified signatures, as there is no Federal Labour Court ruling.
needs.what_good_looks_like: For senders in Germany the product warns on fixed-term employment contracts, terminations and separation agreements that a simple signature is not valid, and says which need wet ink and which could use a qualified signature. HR templates carry the warning by default.

needs.need: UK deeds need a witness who is physically present, and users need the signing flow to capture the witness properly; a remote or missing witness makes the deed invalid.
needs.who: UK small organisations, landlords, charities and directors signing deeds, guarantees and property documents
needs.evidence: Law Commission 2019 report, as summarised by CMS: "the current legal requirement for a deed to be signed "in the presence of a witness" requires the physical presence of that witness" (https://cms.law/en/gbr/legal-updates/law-commission-report-on-the-electronic-execution-of-documents). The same report confirms "an electronic signature is capable of being used to execute a document and it is admissible in evidence" (Mayer Brown note). HM Land Registry practice guide 8 says it continues to require the witness to be actually present when the deed is signed (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/execution-of-deeds/practice-guide-8-execution-of-deeds), and its 2020 blog asks for two-factor authentication "for witnesses as well as signers" (https://hmlandregistry.blog.gov.uk/2020/07/27/electronic-signatures-in-practice/). Electronic Communications Act 2000 section 7 makes electronic signatures admissible in evidence (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2000/7/section/7). Confidence: high on validity and on physical presence; medium on current Land Registry practice, which changed again in June 2026.
needs.what_good_looks_like: A signer can add a witness in the flow. The witness gets a separate one-time code, signs right after the signer and enters name and address into a standard attestation block. The screen states that the witness must be in the same room. Witness steps do not count as an extra paid signature. Wills and lasting powers of attorney are flagged as not suitable.

needs.need: In India a plain e-signature is weaker evidence than an Aadhaar eSign or a digital signature certificate, and users need to be offered the recognised method when the law asks for a signature.
needs.who: Indian small businesses, NGOs, lenders and landlords
needs.evidence: Leegality FAQ: where a law requires a signature, only the IT Act methods (Aadhaar eSign, digital signature certificates) qualify; other electronic methods are acceptable only where no signature is mandated (https://www.leegality.com/blog/esign-estamp-faqs). Adobe's India white paper: with other electronic methods the party relying on the contract must prove it, while for Aadhaar or certificate signatures the burden falls on the challenger (https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/dx-dc/pdf/uk/electronic-signatures-in-india-uk.pdf). Controller of Certifying Authorities brochure: signing is done "using authentication of the Aadhaar holder through Aadhaar e-KYC service" (https://cca.gov.in/sites/files/pdf/esign/esignbrochure1.5.pdf). Zoho Sign offers Aadhaar eSign "in all paid plans and India Data center" and "each Aadhaar eSign signing will consume 2 Zoho Sign Credits" (https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/zoho-sign/general/articles/aadhaar-esign). I could not confirm whether DocuSign supports Aadhaar eSign. Confidence: medium to high; the two-tier position is consistent across sources, but I did not read the Act's Second Schedule itself.
needs.what_good_looks_like: Indian senders can choose Aadhaar eSign per signer as a pay-per-use option with the price shown up front, alongside the normal signature. The product explains in one sentence when each is appropriate, and the audit page records which method was used.

needs.need: An electronic contract is still subject to stamp duty in India and Indonesia; an unstamped agreement can be refused as evidence, and e-signature tools do not mention it.
needs.who: Senders in India (rent agreements, loans, employment bonds) and Indonesia
needs.evidence: Adobe's India white paper and the Leegality FAQ: electronically executed contracts are not exempt from stamp duty; states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Delhi have clarified that electronic records are dutiable; an unstamped instrument is inadmissible in court until duty and a penalty of up to ten times the duty are paid (https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/dx-dc/pdf/uk/electronic-signatures-in-india-uk.pdf, https://www.leegality.com/blog/esign-estamp-faqs). Zoho Sign sells e-stamping in the India data centre (https://www.zoho.com/blog/index.php/sign/pan-india-estamping-with-zoho-sign.html). Indonesia: the tax office sells an electronic duty stamp of Rp10.000 per document, launched 1 October 2021 (https://pajak.go.id/en/node/71611). Confidence: medium; these are secondary sources and duty rules vary by Indian state.
needs.what_good_looks_like: For India and Indonesia the sender is told before sending that the document may need stamp duty and how to attach an e-stamp certificate or e-meterai (upload the stamped first page, or buy through a partner). The product never implies that signing alone makes the document enforceable.

needs.need: In South Africa and Kenya, where a statute requires a signature, only an advanced signature from an accredited provider counts, so an ordinary e-signature silently fails for those documents.
needs.who: South African and Kenyan senders dealing with statutory documents (credit agreements, land, company filings)
needs.evidence: ECTA section 13(1), quoted in De Rebus: "Where the signature of a person is required by law and such law does not specify the type of signature, that requirement in relation to a data message is met only if an advanced electronic signature is used" (https://www.saflii.org/za/journals/DEREBUS/2012/69.html). Werksmans on the Spring Forest case: "required by law" means required by statute, so where the parties themselves require a signature an ordinary electronic signature can suffice. Kenya: "A valid advanced electronic signature can only be issued by a Certification Service Provider (CSP) who is duly licensed by the Communications Authority of Kenya" (commentary on the Business Laws (Amendment) Act 2020, https://cipit.strathmore.edu/?p=4710). Confidence: high for South Africa (statute quoted by several sources and a Supreme Court of Appeal case); medium for Kenya.
needs.what_good_looks_like: A country page and an in-flow hint explain that ordinary commercial contracts are fine with a simple signature, while documents where a statute demands a signature need an accredited advanced signature or wet ink. Sale of land and long leases are flagged.

needs.need: Brazilian users need to know when a non-ICP-Brasil signature is valid and when a qualified ICP-Brasil certificate is mandatory, and the signing flow should record that the parties accepted the method.
needs.who: Brazilian small businesses, landlords, accountants and NGOs
needs.evidence: Lei 14.063/2020: the qualified signature is "a que utiliza certificado digital, nos termos do § 1º do art. 10 da Medida Provisória nº 2.200-2"; the advanced one "utiliza certificados não emitidos pela ICP-Brasil ou outro meio de comprovação da autoria e da integridade"; qualified is required "nos atos de transferência e de registro de bens imóveis" (https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2019-2022/2020/lei/l14063.htm). MP 2.200-2 article 10 paragraph 2 allows other means of proving authorship and integrity if admitted by the "partes como válido ou aceito pela pessoa a quem for oposto o documento" (https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/mpv/Antigas_2001/2200-2.htm). Confidence: high on the three levels and on paragraph 2; medium on real estate, since Lei 14.620/2023 added article 17-A allowing advanced signatures for some property acts and I could not confirm the current rule.
needs.what_good_looks_like: The Portuguese signing flow includes a short clause in which each party accepts the electronic method, which is recorded on the audit page. A CPF or CNPJ field is available for signers. Property transfers and dealings with public bodies trigger a note that an ICP-Brasil certificate may be required.

needs.need: Australian users need to know which documents fall outside the electronic transactions rules (some wills, witnessed deeds, exempt Commonwealth laws) and how companies sign validly online.
needs.who: Australian small companies, sole traders, community groups
needs.evidence: Attorney-General's Department: exemptions from the Electronic Transactions Act 1999 are listed in the Electronic Transactions Regulations 2020, and an exemption does not automatically mean paper must be used (https://ag.gov.au/legal-system/electronic-signatures-documents-and-transactions/exemptions-eta). The explanatory statement says the 2020 Regulations contain 93 exemptions, down from 147. Johnson Winter Slattery (2017): in Victoria, Western Australia and Tasmania "wills cannot be validly executed by electronic signature", and "the types of exemptions are different in each State or Territory" (https://jws.com.au/insights/articles/2017-articles/signing-documents-in-the-digital-age). Confidence: medium; the Commonwealth position is from the official page, but the state rules on wills and deeds come from a 2017 article and have changed since.
needs.what_good_looks_like: An Australia page states the Commonwealth rule, lists the state-level exceptions with dates, and the flow supports two officers signing for a company and a witness step. The product does not claim wills can be signed with it.

needs.need: EU and UK buyers must show where documents are stored and have a data processing agreement, and on small plans they cannot easily get EU hosting, a signed agreement, or a clear statement of what data goes to the US.
needs.who: EU and UK small organisations with a data protection officer, public-sector or health customers, or clients who ask
needs.evidence: DocuSign's data residency page says that once the region is set, "eDocuments are stored only within DocuSign data centers in that region", but also that some data is shared between the U.S. and E.U. instances, including account identity information (https://www.docusign.com/content/data-residency). A competitor's compliance scan states DocuSign is subject to the CLOUD Act and FISA 702 and that compliant use needs a processing agreement, standard contractual clauses and a transfer impact assessment (https://scan.meetergo.com/en/vendors/docusign). European directories list Yousign, Scrive, Skribble and sproof as the usual substitutes (https://european-alternatives.eu/alternative-to/docusign). Note: I found vendor pages only, no first-hand buyer complaint, so frequency is an estimate.
needs.what_good_looks_like: EU hosting can be chosen at sign-up on the $9 plan. A processing agreement with standard clauses is accepted in one click and downloadable as a PDF. A public page lists every subprocessor with country and purpose and says exactly which data leaves the region. Retention and deletion of signed documents are under the customer's control.

needs.need: Prices and invoices are in US dollars or a currency fixed at sign-up that cannot be changed later, so buyers pay conversion fees and cannot budget in their own currency.
needs.who: Small organisations in the euro area, UK, Australia, India, Brazil and Africa
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community employee reply (February 2024, thread about an invoice showing no currency and a request for euros; found by searching community.docusign.com, exact thread URL not confirmed): "Usually, when creating an account you select the needed currency and sadly once the account is created, it can not be changed. You would need to create a new account if you want the currency to reflect the needed one." Capterra's India page lists DocuSign plans in dollars only (https://www.capterra.in/reviews/121506/docusign), and reviewers there and on the UK and Australian pages call it too expensive for a few documents a month. I found no review that complains specifically about dollar-only pricing.
needs.what_good_looks_like: The price is shown and charged in the buyer's currency for the main markets (EUR, GBP, AUD, INR, BRL, ZAR and others), with the currency printed on every invoice. Currency can be changed in billing settings without opening a new account. Where only dollars are possible, the checkout says so before the card is entered.

needs.need: Subscription card payments from outside the US fail: Indian cards are declined for recurring charges under Reserve Bank rules, and checkouts reject valid foreign cards with no reason given.
needs.who: Buyers in India first of all; also buyers elsewhere whose banks block foreign recurring charges
needs.evidence: Adobe help page title: "Payment declined due to Reserve Bank of India's mandate" (https://helpx.adobe.com/in/account/individual/subscriptions-and-plans/renewals-and-cancellations/payment-declined-reserve-bank-of-indias-mandate.html). Stripe docs: without a mandate an off-session payment "will be declined" (https://docs.stripe.com/india-recurring-payments). LinkedIn help: "if you're using a credit card issued in India or making transactions in a non-INR currency, you may experience higher approval failures" (https://www.linkedin.com/help/billing/answer/a515185). DocuSign Community thread title: "checkout error we re unable to place your order can t purchase after free trial every payment method fails", with the error text "We're unable to place your order at this time. Please try again. If the problem continues, contact support." (https://community.docusign.com/general-discussion-145/checkout-error-we-re-unable-to-place-your-order-can-t-purchase-after-free-trial-every-payment-method-fails-27276).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Checkout supports card authentication and Indian e-mandates, plus at least one local method per main market (UPI, SEPA debit, PIX). A prepaid pack of signatures can be bought as a one-off payment, which avoids recurring-charge rules. A failed payment shows the real reason and never locks the account out of its signed documents.

needs.need: Name fields assume a Western first name and last name: names get split at the first space, family-name-first order is broken, and signers cannot fix how their name appears.
needs.who: Signers in Japan, China, Indonesia, South India and anyone with one name, several given names or a compound surname
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread "help needed displaying full name in docusign for japanese signers": the adopt-signature window shows first and last name instead of the full name, and the split came out as "'Jhon' as the First Name and '(ドウ' as the Last Name" (https://community.docusign.com/workday-36/help-needed-displaying-full-name-in-docusign-for-japanese-signers-22245). Idea thread: "DocuSign Doesn't provide today any functionality in configuration to manage how the Full Name should looks like" (https://community.docusign.com/ideas/format-of-full-name-build-from-first-name-and-last-name-27736). Adobe Community: the web form "only provides a single box and assumes that everything before the first space is their first name" (https://community.adobe.com/questions-35/web-form-signer-info-fields-for-name-are-unreliable-20349).
needs.what_good_looks_like: One free-text full name field everywhere, stored and printed exactly as typed, in any script and any order. No required last name. The signer can correct their own name before signing and the audit page shows both the name the sender typed and the name the signer confirmed.

needs.need: Text typed in non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Khmer, Arabic, Cyrillic) shows as empty boxes or unreadable characters in fields, typed signatures or the final PDF.
needs.who: Signers and senders in East and South-East Asia, the Middle East and Eastern Europe
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread "docusign doesn t recognize khmer font", staff reply: "the current font selection is limited to the list provided below" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/docusign-doesn-t-recognize-khmer-font-4194). Thread "simplified chinese character display issue": text was correct before upload and after download but wrong inside DocuSign (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/simplified-chinese-character-display-issue-1148). Odoo forum thread title: "in sign module when i download the document after the client signed it the document shows me black squares in arabic fields" (https://www.odoo.com/nl_NL/forum/help-1/in-sign-module-when-i-download-the-document-after-the-client-signed-it-the-document-shows-me-black-squares-in-arabic-fields-in-odoo-14-can-anyone-help-231412). Dropbox Sign help: "not all languages are supported in text fields" (https://help.dropbox.com/view-edit/supported-languages-text-fields-dropbox-sign).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Every text field, typed signature style and the audit page use fonts with full Unicode coverage and embed them in the final PDF. A release test signs a document with Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Khmer, Hindi, Arabic, Hebrew and Cyrillic names and checks the output. If a chosen signature font lacks the characters, a matching font is used automatically.

needs.need: Right-to-left text (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian) typed into fields is reversed, disappears or is left-aligned, and competitors treat direction as a manual per-field setting.
needs.who: Signers and senders in the Middle East, North Africa and Israel
needs.evidence: Adobe help page title: "Hebrew or Arabic text entered using Fill & Sign gets reversed when you save" (https://helpx.adobe.com/acrobat/kb/hebrew-text-gets-reversed-fill-and-sign.html). Adobe Community thread title: "hebrew or any rtl text in form field disappears unless you click on it" (https://community.adobe.com/questions-9/hebrew-or-any-rtl-text-in-form-field-disappears-unless-you-click-on-it-1238617). BoldSign documents a per-field option, with the API text direction defaulting to left-to-right (https://support.boldsign.com/kb/article/13253/align-text-in-the-form-fields-from-right-to-left). I found no DocuSign-specific complaint, so this rests on Adobe and BoldSign material.
needs.what_good_looks_like: Field direction is detected from what the signer types. The signing interface is mirrored when the language is Arabic or Hebrew. Mixed text (Arabic with numbers or Latin words) is stored and printed in the correct order in the final PDF.

needs.need: The stronger identity checks offered by US vendors only work for people with a US Social Security Number, so senders have no equivalent for signers elsewhere.
needs.who: Senders anywhere whose signers are outside the US; non-US senders shopping for identity checks
needs.evidence: Adobe help: knowledge-based authentication "is only valid for vetting the identity of US-based recipients" and is "available to the business and enterprise service plans only" (https://helpx.adobe.com/sign/using/adobesign-authentication-kba.html). PandaDoc: "KBA is available only for US citizens, as it requires a Social Security Number (SSN)" (https://support.pandadoc.com/en/articles/9715010-knowledge-based-authentication-kba). Zoho Sign: KBA "is only valid for verifying the identity of signers who hold the US social security number" (https://help.zoho.com/portal/en/kb/zoho-sign/general/articles/kba-in-zoho-sign).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Identity options are country-neutral by default: email link plus a one-time code by SMS, WhatsApp or email, and optionally a photo of a government ID. Any method that only works in one country is labelled with that country and never presented as the standard secure choice.

needs.need: Reminder emails go out at a fixed hour in the middle of the night and expiry times are not shown in the recipient's zone, so signers abroad get messages at 1am and miss deadlines.
needs.who: Senders and signers outside the Americas
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community: reminders are "sent near midnight/1am local time, depending on time zone and whether it is daylight savings time or not"; a user suggests "changing the hard-coded middle of the night time to noon or 1PM would solve the problem"; staff reply: "there is currently no option or setting in DocuSign that allows for the Reminders to be sent within certain working hours or other time criteria" (https://community.docusign.com/ideas/ability-to-choose-the-time-of-day-reminders-are-sent-23290 and https://community.docusign.com/ideas/allow-setting-time-and-time-zone-when-sending-reminders-26713). On expiry, DocuSign says the shown time is when the envelope "enters the expiration process" and it "can take up to 24 hours from this time to expire" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-111/envelope-expiration-date-time-1452).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Reminders are sent during the recipient's working hours, with the zone taken from the recipient's last visit or else the sender's zone. The sender can pick the time. Every deadline is shown with date, time and zone, and expiry happens at that exact moment.

needs.need: Many signers outside North America and Europe live in WhatsApp or SMS, not email, and delivery by those channels is a paid add-on on higher plans.
needs.who: Senders in Latin America, India, Africa and South-East Asia whose customers have no working email
needs.evidence: DocuSign's own launch material says WhatsApp is the most popular messaging tool in 100+ countries (https://www.docusign.com/company/press-room/docusign-launches-whatsapp-integration-to-accelerate-business-around-the-globe). TechRadar reports the add-on is for Standard customers and above and that SMS and WhatsApp delivery "costs $0.40 per agreement" (https://www.techradar.com/pro/you-can-now-finalize-a-docusign-signing-on-whatsapp). DocuSign's developer blog: "WhatsApp delivery is a standalone delivery method and does not work in tandem with email or SMS", limited to five WhatsApp recipients per envelope (https://www.docusign.com/blog/developers/whatsapp-joins-docusign-multi-channel-delivery). These are vendor sources; I found no first-hand user complaint.
needs.what_good_looks_like: Every signing request has a link and a QR code the sender can paste into WhatsApp or any messenger at no extra charge. A signer can be invited with a phone number alone. The signing page works on a low-end phone over a slow connection, and the completed copy can be downloaded without an email address.

needs.need: Signers in mainland China cannot load or finish the signing page, and the vendor's advice is to use a VPN.
needs.who: Senders with suppliers, customers or staff in mainland China
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread (August 2024) about a client in China: "They are having trouble opening and accessing the documents for e-signature."; a DocuSign employee suggested clearing the cache, another browser or network, and a VPN (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/can-a-signer-in-china-use-docusign-20002). Adobe Acrobat Sign restricted its service in China from 13 October 2025 (https://devicepartner.microsoft.com/de-ch/communications/comm-adobe-acrobat-sign-service-restriction-china-effective-october-2025).
needs.what_good_looks_like: The signing page loads no resources from domains that are blocked in China (fonts, captchas, analytics, maps) and is tested from a mainland connection. If the page cannot load, the invitation email explains a fallback, such as downloading the PDF and returning a signed copy.

needs.need: Number and money fields assume a decimal point and a dollar sign; European formats such as 1.234,56 are rejected, reset to US format or break calculations.
needs.who: Senders in continental Europe and Latin America who put prices or amounts in forms
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread: number tabs made in the web UI keep the German locale so that "the signing view shows 1.234,56", but the locale is replaced by en-US when the same tab is placed by anchor text (https://community.docusign.com/developer-tools-175/localepolicy-culturename-of-numerical-tabs-is-replaced-by-en-us-when-the-tab-is-placed-with-anchorstring-kept-original-with-fixed-position-27992). In DocuSign CLM a sum only works with "a dot (.) as the decimal separator" (https://community.docusign.com/clm-112/how-to-sum-table-rows-with-xpath-and-format-the-number-25085). Adobe Community thread title: "decimal separator not respecting locale in adobe sign forms" (https://community.adobe.com/questions-35/decimal-separator-not-respecting-locale-in-adobe-sign-forms-18059).
needs.what_good_looks_like: Number and currency fields follow the document's locale for input and display, the currency symbol is chosen per field with no dollar default, and any calculation works on the parsed value so both 1.234,56 and 1,234.56 are handled correctly.

needs.need: Signature fields move or documents are rescaled when the page is not the size the tool expects, which hits A4 users working with Letter-based templates and tools.
needs.who: Senders outside North America, where A4 is the standard paper size
needs.evidence: DocuSign Community thread title: "how to set up a tag so it doesn t move if the pdf used with the template is in different size with each signing"; the answer recommends "converting documents to a consistent PDF format, like Letter or A4, will help ensure the fields stay exactly where you expect" (https://community.docusign.com/docusign-admin-102/how-to-set-up-a-tag-so-it-doesn-t-move-if-the-pdf-used-with-the-template-is-in-different-size-with-each-signing-26094). A DocuSign employee says odd rendering mostly happens when "the document resolution is too big (above the recommended A4/Letter size)" (https://community.docusign.com/esignature-171/how-to-enlarge-pages-and-signature-boxes-when-options-do-not-work-23127). Weak evidence: I found no complaint that names A4 being converted to Letter.
needs.what_good_looks_like: The signed PDF keeps the original page size of every page. Template field positions are stored relative to the page, so they stay put on A4 and Letter alike. The audit page is generated in the same size as the document, A4 for an A4 contract.

needs.need: Mexican businesses expect a NOM-151 conservation certificate with a signed contract to prove its date and integrity, and a tool without it looks incomplete to them.
needs.who: Mexican companies, accountants and HR teams
needs.evidence: Dropbox Sign has a help page on NOM-151 compliance and offers a NOM-151 option on signature requests through a partner (https://help.dropbox.com/es-es/security/dropbox-sign-nom-151). DocuSign Mexico: to comply with NOM-151, "siempre son utilizados los servicios de un PSC validado para emitir la constancia de conservación" (https://www.docusign.com/es-mx/blog/nom-151). Sources agree the certificate strengthens proof and that a document does not automatically lose validity without it. The norm is NOM-151-SCFI-2016 (https://dof.gob.mx/normasOficiales/6499/seeco11_C/seeco11_C.html). Confidence: medium; the norm exists and vendors sell compliance, but how often a small organisation truly needs it is not established.
needs.what_good_looks_like: A Mexican sender can add a NOM-151 certificate to a document as an optional paid extra from an accredited provider, and the Spanish audit page shows it. The Mexico page explains in two sentences what it is and when it matters.

needs.need: When a qualified signature is used, the name the sender typed must match the signer's identity document exactly, and common variations (married name plus birth name, extra given names) make the identification fail.
needs.who: EU senders who need a qualified signature and their signers
needs.evidence: Yousign developer docs, "Signer name parsing rules for the QES level": the declared last name must match the birth name or the usage name, and declaring both together "will result in a failed identification"; "the identity declared by the Sender and the identity on the ID document must strictly match" (https://developers.yousign.com/docs/signer-name-parsing-rules-for-the-qes-level). Yousign's help centre adds that "not all identification documents (e.g., passports, national ID cards, and residence permits) are eligible for QES verification" (https://help.youtrust.com/en/articles/273289-accepted-id-documents-for-qualified-electronic-signature-qes).
needs.what_good_looks_like: If a qualified signature is ever offered through a partner, the signer confirms or corrects their own legal name against their document before the check, the accepted documents per country are shown first, and a failed check does not consume a paid signature.
